picks.rationale: The boldest shipping attempt yet at an AI-first phone interface — AI-assembled widgets replacing app-switching is a live test of a UI paradigm designers keep sketching.
picks.excerpt: Nothing OS 5.0 on Android 17 leans on AI-assembled widgets and glanceable surfaces to keep users out of app-switching — the boldest attempt yet at an AI-first phone interface.

picks.rationale: Local-first with an explicit consent prompt before any cloud call — a concrete privacy pattern for anyone handling client files on an AI PC.
picks.excerpt: Perplexity's Portable Computer keeps files and AI tasks on your own hardware, only reaching for a cloud model when you explicitly allow it — a local-first posture for everyday PC AI.

picks.rationale: The single best card from the M6/M5 Mac wave: a 2nm chip with a dual 16-core Neural Engine resets what creative tools can run locally on a consumer Mac.
picks.excerpt: Apple announced the M6, its first 2nm chip, with a dual 16-core Neural Engine and a 12-core CPU. The on-device AI budget in a consumer Mac jumps again, which is what changes what creative tools can run locally.

picks.rationale: Reverse-engineering closed gear in hours to build your own controls is the most directly copyable workflow here — and the security caveat comes from the engineer himself.
picks.excerpt: An Amazon security engineer used Claude Opus to reverse-engineer Asus, Insta360 and Elgato gear in hours and build better controls for it — a glimpse of AI as a gadget-modding tool, and a security worry.

picks.rationale: An information-design shift on the wrist: Garmin Epic stitches an outing into one narrative instead of a metrics dump, which is the harder half of wearable AI.
picks.excerpt: Garmin's Fenix 9 and 9 Pro add Garmin Epic, which stitches multiple activities into one holistic narrative of an outing rather than a pile of disconnected metrics.
